ask.where: Only this web app gets it. You can change it later in Settings → Web Apps.
desc.chat: Messages and groups, in a window of its own
desc.teamwork: Chat, meetings and calls for teams
desc.social: Photos, videos and messages from the people you follow
desc.ideas: Ideas and inspiration, saved to boards
desc.files: Your files in the cloud, shared with others
desc.documents: Documents you write and edit together
desc.boards: Boards and cards to organize work
desc.cloud: Mail, photos, files and notes in the cloud
desc.assistant: An assistant to ask, write and think with
desc.photos: Your photos and videos, backed up and organized
store.subtitle: A web app opens in a window of its own, with its icon in the Dock. Each one can have several accounts (profiles), each with its own data.
store.whatHappens: It opens in a window of its own, apart from your browser and from the other web apps. It asks before it uses the camera, the microphone, the screen or your location.
store.untested: Not checked on LordOS yet: some features may not work.
store.installed: {name} is installed. It's in Apps, and you can keep it in the Dock.
store.addHint: LordOS opens the page apart, without any of your data, to read its name and icon. Nothing is installed until you press Install.
store.name: Name
store.badName: Give it a name of up to 64 characters.
store.manifestYes: The site describes itself as a web app.
store.manifestNo: The site doesn't describe itself as a web app: it opens as a page in a window of its own.
store.address.scheme: Only secure (https) addresses can be added.
store.address.invalid: That doesn't look like a web address.
settings.noRuntime: The lordos-web package isn't installed, so web apps can't open. The Store's Web apps section installs it.
settings.footer: Choose an app to see its profiles, its permissions and how much space it takes.
settings.none: No web apps installed. Get them in the Store.
settings.profilesFooter: Each profile is a separate account, with its own data, cookies and window. The Dock opens the first one; the others are in its right-click menu.
settings.badName: A name of 1 to 64 characters, with no space at either end.
settings.permissionsFooter: Ask: the app asks the first time it needs it, and your answer shows here.
settings.backgroundFooter: Closing the window keeps the app running behind its icon next to the clock, so its notifications still arrive. Quit it from that icon.
settings.wipeOn: Its data goes too: the signed-in session, what the site saved on this computer and its cookies.
settings.wipeOff: Its data stays on this computer: adding it again with the same name brings it back.
store.engineTitle: LordOS's web engine isn't installed yet
store.engineBody: Web apps run in LordOS's own web engine (the lordos-web package). The first app you get installs it too, once; the rest of LordOS works the same without it.
get.engineTitle: LordOS's web engine is needed once
get.engineBody: {name} runs in LordOS's own web engine (the lordos-web package), which isn't installed yet. It's installed once, with this app; the next web apps don't need it.
get.enginePlanFailed: The engine can't be installed now: check the package lists in Updates.
get.thenApp: Then {name} is installed, with no other click.
discover.title: Your web services, as apps
discover.text: {names} and more: each in a window of its own, with its icon in the Dock and as many accounts as you want.
detail.notFound: This web app isn't in the list or installed anymore.
detail.sourceAddress: Added by you from an address
detail.engineMissing: LordOS Web: installed with the first web app
detail.permissionsBefore: Before installing, it asks you each time; you can change it in Settings → Web Apps.
detail.limitsUnknown: Not known: LordOS hasn't checked this site.
limit.drm: Protected music and video (DRM) can't play in LordOS's web engine.
limit.calls: Voice and video calls may not work yet.
limit.push: Notifications arrive only while the app runs: keep it in the background to get them.
limit.theme: If the site stays light when the desktop is dark, choose Dark in the site's own Settings → Theme.
settings.trayHint: Its icon next to the clock, with Open and Quit. Running in the background does not need it.
settings.badge: Show unread count on the Dock
settings.badgeHint: The number the site counts, on the app’s icon (the sum of its profiles).
settings.dockPerProfile: Each profile has its own Dock icon
settings.dockPerProfileHint: While a profile other than the first is open, it gets an icon of its own with its color.
settings.notifySoundFooter: LordOS controls only its own sound. To turn off the sound the site itself plays, use the site’s own settings.
settings.moreNotify: Banners, alerts and Do Not Disturb
settings.iconTile: LordOS’s letter tile (the site’s icon is fetched when the app opens)
sound.autoHint: LordOS’s sound only when the site plays none of its own.
sound.appHint: Only the sound the site plays.
sound.noneHint: No sound from LordOS (the site may still play its own).
